incidents.name: PHP-CGI argument injection on Windows
incidents.note: Only PHP run as CGI behind Apache on Windows, in certain code pages. Exploited in the wild within days; in CISA KEV.

incidents.name: Heartbleed
incidents.note: Reads server or client memory over TLS, including private keys. Exploited in the wild; in CISA KEV.

incidents.name: CMS AuthEnvelopedData stack overflow
incidents.note: Reachable without a key where the product parses untrusted CMS or PKCS#7 data (S/MIME, for example). Fixed in the January 2026 OpenSSL releases.

incidents.name: Java4Shell (HotSpot AVX-512 Base64 decoder heap overflow)
incidents.note: Only on x86-64 CPUs with AVX-512 VBMI (Intel Ice Lake and later Xeons and some Core chips, AMD Zen 4 and later); ARM64 is not affected. Also affected: Oracle Java SE 8 Enterprise Performance Pack 8u511b33-perf (fixed in 8u513-perf) and GraalVM Enterprise Edition 21.3.20.0.3. Interim mitigations (either one): -XX:-UseBASE64Intrinsics (preferred; VulnCheck tested it with -XX:+UnlockDiagnosticVMOptions ahead of it), or -XX:UseAVX=2 on x86-64 hosts only, since JVMs on ARM64 fail to start with it. A proof of concept that triggers the bug is public, and probing and exploit attempts have been seen since 18 November (GreyNoise, watchTowr); no confirmed compromise and not in CISA KEV as of 2026-11-19.

incidents.name: NGINX2Root
incidents.note: CVE-2026-123007 (HTTP/2, unauthenticated) is the remote code execution entry point; the disclosure chains it with an unpatched Linux kernel SCTP bug to reach root. Disabling HTTP/2 blocks only CVE-2026-123007 and CVE-2026-123633. A proof of concept for CVE-2026-123007 is public (Rapid7); not in CISA KEV as of 2026-11-19.

incidents.name: Tomcat partial PUT remote code execution
JSP upload through HTTP PUT
incidents.note: Needs HTTP PUT enabled (readonly=false on the Default servlet). Exploited in the wild; in CISA KEV.

incidents.name: EncryptInterceptor bypass
incidents.note: Affects clusters that rely on EncryptInterceptor, and only these three releases. In CISA KEV since August 2026.

incidents.name: May 2026 HTTP/2, DIGEST and security-constraint fixes
incidents.note: Scored critical by CVSS, though Apache rates them low to moderate. Exploits are public, and the fixes set off advisories from Atlassian, Ubuntu and others. Tomcat 8.5 is affected and gets no fix.

incidents.name: Jolokia MBean remote code execution
incidents.note: Needs a login to the web console's Jolokia API. In CISA KEV since April 2026.

incidents.name: Struts file upload path traversal (S2-066, S2-067)
OGNL and REST plugin remote code execution (S2-052, S2-057, S2-061)
incidents.note: All three are exploited in the wild and in CISA KEV. Each needs a condition: the REST plugin (2017), alwaysSelectFullNamespace (2018), or forced OGNL evaluation of user input in tag attributes (2020).

incidents.name: mod_rewrite filesystem mapping (code execution or source disclosure)
incidents.note: Needs mod_rewrite rules whose substitution starts with a backreference or variable. Exploited in the wild; in CISA KEV.

incidents.name: Axis 1.x SOAP fault class instantiation RCE
incidents.note: Unauthenticated remote class instantiation through a crafted SOAP fault. Axis 1.x is end of life with no upstream fix; CISA added it to KEV on 18 November 2026. Rapid7 saw it exploited against Confluence Data Center (with the SOAP remote API on) and N-able N-central (with the Legacy API on) from 13 November; a Metasploit module followed on 17 November.

incidents.name: inflate() gzip header extra-field overflow
incidents.note: Only applications that call inflateGetHeader are affected. It set off advisories from most vendors that bundle zlib; proof-of-concept code is public.

incidents.name: Expat 2.4.5 parser memory corruption
incidents.note: Reachable by parsing untrusted XML. Triggered advisories across vendors that bundle Expat.

incidents.name: Variable-font subglyph out-of-bounds write
incidents.note: Exploited in the wild; in CISA KEV since May 2025. Triggered by parsing a crafted font.

incidents.name: Server authentication bypass
incidents.note: Only products that use libssh as an SSH server are exposed; clients are not. Public exploits exist.

incidents.name: Daemon checksum-length heap overflow
incidents.note: Reachable by anyone who can connect to an rsync daemon with anonymous read access. One of six rsync bugs disclosed together in January 2025; fixed in 3.4.0.

incidents.name: SambaCry
incidents.note: Needs a share the attacker can write to. Exploited in the wild; in CISA KEV.

incidents.name: DNSpooq
incidents.note: The two memory-corruption bugs of the DNSpooq set; both need DNSSEC validation turned on. Proof-of-concept code is public.

incidents.name: VP8 encoder heap overflow
incidents.note: Exploited in the wild through browsers; in CISA KEV. Bundled the same way as libwebp.

incidents.name: Constructor deserialization RCE
incidents.note: Exploitable when the product parses untrusted YAML with the default Constructor. Public exploits exist, and it triggered advisories across Java vendors.

incidents.name: Polymorphic deserialization RCE
incidents.note: The first and one of the last of the 2017-2020 gadget-chain bugs. Exploitable only when the product turns on polymorphic (default) typing for untrusted JSON; public exploits exist.

incidents.name: InvokerTransformer deserialization gadget
incidents.note: The gadget chain behind the 2015 wave of Java deserialization attacks (WebLogic, WebSphere, JBoss, Jenkins). Exploitable where the product deserializes untrusted Java objects; ysoserial has a ready-made payload.

incidents.name: Unmarshalling RCE
incidents.note: Exploited in the wild (VMware NSX Manager and Cloud Foundation); in CISA KEV.

incidents.name: Console JNDI remote code execution
incidents.note: Unauthenticated when the H2 web console is reachable; same JNDI root cause as Log4Shell. Public exploits exist.

incidents.name: Variable interpolation RCE
incidents.note: The same script, dns and url lookups as Text4Shell, reachable when untrusted values are interpolated. Commons Configuration 1.x is not affected.

incidents.name: Simple-query-mode SQL injection
incidents.note: Only with the non-default PreferQueryMode=SIMPLE. Rated 10.0 and patched in six branches at once, which set off advisories across Java vendors.

incidents.name: XFA-in-PDF XML external entity injection
incidents.note: Rated 10.0. Triggered by parsing a crafted PDF; the fix is in tika-core, so updating only the PDF parser module is not enough.

incidents.name: DiskFileItem deserialization RCE
incidents.note: Exploitable where the product deserializes untrusted Java objects; a ysoserial payload exists.

incidents.name: snmptrapd buffer overflow
incidents.note: Only products that run snmptrapd and accept traps from untrusted hosts are exposed. Rated 9.8; proof-of-concept code is public. Distribution packages carry backported fixes.

incidents.name: Class-loader access through the class property
incidents.note: The bug behind the 2014 Struts 1 class-loader attacks (a Metasploit module exists). 1.9.4 was the first release to block the class property by default.

incidents.name: declaredClass property access on enums
incidents.note: Exploitable where property paths come from untrusted input. Triggered advisories across Java vendors in 2025.

incidents.name: MethodClosure deserialization gadget
incidents.note: Exploitable where the product deserializes untrusted Java objects with Groovy on the classpath; ysoserial has a payload.

incidents.name: RegexRequestMatcher authorization bypass
incidents.note: Only applications that use RegexRequestMatcher with a dot in the pattern. Rated 9.8; proof-of-concept code is public.

incidents.name: Pipe-device and format-string sandbox escapes
incidents.note: Code execution from a crafted PostScript, EPS or PDF file, which matters where the product converts or prints untrusted documents. Public exploits exist for both.

incidents.name: ImageTragick
incidents.note: Command injection from a crafted image where the product converts untrusted uploads. Exploited in the wild; in CISA KEV.
